channel.title: The Grant Desk - Media Arts, Film & Sound, Africa
channel.description: Paid open calls, fellowships and residencies in AI, tech, research, and digital and mixed-media arts, sorted into the right pile. Updated as new calls land on the desk. Filtered to: Media Arts, Film & Sound, Africa.

item.title: Marrakech IFF: Atlas Station 2026 (Short Film Track)
item.description:
Organisation: Festival International du Film de Marrakech (Atlas Workshops)

Location: Online in October 2026, then onsite in Marrakech, Morocco, 22-26 November 2026. Open to Moroccan directors only.

Award: No application fee. Participation in the online and onsite professional programme is covered.

Duration: Five-day online programme in October 2026, followed by a five-day onsite programme 22-26 November 2026.

Deadline: 14 Sep 2026

The short film strand of Atlas Station, the Marrakech International Film Festival's professional development programme for the Moroccan film industry, running alongside the 9th Atlas Workshops. Selected directors receive mentoring and industry access during the online and onsite sessions. ELIGIBILITY IS RESTRICTED: open to Moroccan directors with a short film in shooting or post-production that has not yet premiered. Not open to international applicants. Deadline 14 September 2026.

item.title: Marrakech IFF: Atlas Station 2026 (Producers Track)
item.description:
Organisation: Festival International du Film de Marrakech (Atlas Workshops)

Location: Online in October 2026, then onsite in Marrakech, Morocco, 22-26 November 2026. Open to Moroccan producers only.

Award: No application fee. Participation in the online and onsite professional programme is covered.

Duration: Five-day online programme in October 2026, followed by a five-day onsite programme 22-26 November 2026.

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

Atlas Station is the Marrakech International Film Festival's professional development strand running alongside the Atlas Workshops, aimed at building the Moroccan film industry. The producers track offers structured mentoring, industry sessions and access to the festival's international network during the 9th edition. ELIGIBILITY IS RESTRICTED: open to Moroccan producers only, not to international applicants. Deadline 31 August 2026. See also the Atlas Station short film track (deadline 14 September 2026) and the internationally open Atlas Workshops track for films in shooting or post-production.

item.title: Gallery 1957: Yaa Asantewaa Art Prize 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Gallery 1957

Location: Accra, Ghana and Saint-Louis / Dakar, Senegal. Open to female citizens of Ghana or Senegal residing in either country or in the diaspora.

Award: USD 5,000 cash per winner, two winners (one Ghanaian, one Senegalese), plus a fully covered three-month residency exchange: flights, transportation of artworks, accommodation and materials. No application fee.

Duration: Three-month residency exchange. The Ghanaian winner spends one month in Saint-Louis and two months in Dakar; the Senegalese winner spends three months in Accra.

Deadline: 30 Sep 2026

Annual prize from Gallery 1957 in Accra for women artists connected to Ghana and to Senegal, which joins the prize for the first time in 2026. Two winners are selected, one from each country, and each receives USD 5,000 in cash, a three-month residency exchange in the partner country with flights, artwork transport, accommodation and materials covered, and a resulting exhibition with the gallery. ELIGIBILITY IS GEOGRAPHICALLY RESTRICTED: applicants must be female citizens of Ghana or Senegal, aged 18 or over, living in Ghana, Senegal or the diaspora, and must present a valid national ID or passport. Not open to international applicants without that citizenship. Apply by email to applications@gallery1957.com with an artist bio or statement of no more than 200 words and a portfolio of up to six high-resolution images or videos with captions, both as PDFs. Questions go to awo@gallery1957.com. Deadline 30 September 2026.

Open call details

item.title: Marrakech IFF: Atlas Workshops 2026 (Films in Shooting or Post-Production)
item.description:
Organisation: Festival International du Film de Marrakech (Atlas Workshops)

Location: Online in October 2026, then onsite in Marrakech, Morocco, 22-26 November 2026, alongside the Marrakech International Film Festival.

Award: No application fee. Participation in the online and onsite programme is covered. Cash prizes are awarded by a dedicated jury at the close of the Workshops; the festival does not publish the prize amounts on the call page.

Duration: Five-day online programme in October 2026, followed by a five-day onsite programme 22-26 November 2026.

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

The Atlas Workshops are the Marrakech International Film Festival's industry and talent-development programme, running since 2018 and now in its 9th edition. This track is for feature films already in shooting or post-production. Selected teams get personalised mentoring tailored to each project across scriptwriting, production, distribution, editing and scoring, plus access to the festival's industry network, and compete for cash prizes decided by a dedicated jury. ELIGIBILITY: directors and producers who are from, or in the diaspora of, the Arab world or the African continent, working on their first, second or third feature (fiction, documentary or animation), with a production company attached. Open across that whole region, not restricted to Morocco. There is a separate Projects in Development track whose deadline (6 July 2026) has already passed for this edition. Deadline 31 August 2026.

Open call details

item.title: EUNIC: Spaces of Culture 2026 (Call for Proposals)
item.description:
Organisation: EUNIC (European Union National Institutes for Culture)

Location: Sub-Saharan Africa; requires a triangular partnership of at least three local cultural/civil-society organisations, full EUNIC members, and EU Delegation participation

Award: Up to EUR 50,000 per project; minimum 5 percent co-funding required from partners. Projects implemented 1 September 2026 to 31 August 2027.

Duration: Projects run 1 September 2026 to 31 August 2027

Deadline: Closed 21 Jun 2026

The second Spaces of Culture call supports new, contemporary and innovative cultural relations projects in Sub-Saharan Africa, co-created through equitable partnership and mutual dialogue. THEMES: arts, creative industries, digitalisation, education, gender, heritage, human rights, social inclusion, sports, sustainability, tourism, youth and more. STRUCTURE: each project must be jointly defined and co-developed by a triangular partnership comprising at least three local cultural/civil-society organisations, at least three full EUNIC members (or two if no local cluster exists), and EU Delegation participation. FUNDING: up to EUR 50,000 per project, with a minimum 5 percent co-funding contribution from partners; projects implemented between 1 September 2026 and 31 August 2027. APPLY: submit the application form template, an estimated budget (in EUR) and partner support letters, in English, to spacesofculture@eunicglobal.eu by 21 June 2026 (23:59 CAT). Queries: robert.kieft@eunicglobal.eu or thoriso.moseneke@eunicglobal.eu.

Open call details
